\newcommand{\method}{RepRoute}

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:intro}

In today's rapidly evolving landscape of large language models, multimodal web
agents delve into increasingly complex tasks --- from simple navigation to
sophisticated reasoning. It is worth noting that representation routing plays a
pivotal role in this paradigm, serving as a testament to the power of selective
classification. The routing decision boundary is a simple threshold,
$y = x + 1$, which underscores the importance of the cost-accuracy trade-off.

Prior work has delved into routing for web agents~\cite{wang2025routing}.
Benchmark studies of multi-step tool use report similar cost
profiles~\cite{chen2024agents} (see pp.~10--12 of the supplement).

Our method \method{} achieves 92\% accuracy. Representation routing reduces
inference cost by 4.23\% on average (11.58\% in the best case), with median
routing latency of 5 ms, as described in Section~\ref{sec:method}. Ablating
the router shifts accuracy by -0.8 points (p = .05).
